=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5525-5528,5560-5564 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: When `_close_sweep_check_triage_branch` returns rc=2 because the marker-PR read failed, the candidate is still logged as `rejected=non_target_base base=...` and `sweep_non_target_seen=true` is set, even though the real cause is `check_triage_pr_fetch_failed`.
  WHY: The sweep still defers the issue correctly through `sweep_pr_fetch_failed=true`, but the logs blame the wrong cause and hide why the candidate was skipped; both reviewers rated it NIT.
- scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:2918-2923 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The completion rule assumes the CHECK_TRIAGE_ISSUES_TOKEN and GH_PAT identities match, but the repository does not require or verify that. When they belong to different accounts, both completion paths reject the issue author (issue_pr_status.yml:230-234 and orchestrate_poll_process.sh:4138-4143 resolve the login using GH_PAT; check_failure_triage.yml:684-687 creates triage issues using CHECK_TRIAGE_ISSUES_TOKEN; README.md:64 describes it as a separate token).
  WHY: check_triage_target_branch returns None when the author does not match, so the PR-close path leaves the issue unchanged, the sweep treats it as pending, and a successfully merged fix does not close the triage issue (source severity MAJOR).
- tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py:(no line given) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The test suite in tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py is failing, indicating regressions or incorrect test setup.
  WHY: The newly added unit tests for triage logic do not pass, which prevents verification of the implemented requirements and blocks safe deployment (source severity MAJOR).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:(no line given) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Linting tools report shell syntax errors.
  WHY: Syntax errors in shell scripts make execution fail during orchestrator poll cycles, so the sweep fails (source severity MAJOR).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:(no line given) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The third candidate list (ai:check-triage) adds a timeline read for each issue on every tick, up to 200 issues.
  WHY: This adds significant load to the orchestrator poll process and may cause timeouts during poll cycles when many triage issues are open (source severity MAJOR).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Security: trust the marker only when the issue author is the pipeline login, as other pipeline-authored markers are trusted. The marker PR must have a same-repository head. Compare against `head.ref` from the API, never from issue text." (from linked issue #8955)
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_lib.py:check_triage_target_branch (author/pipeline_login comparison at lines 2920-2923) and the corresponding trust gate at .github/workflows/issue_pr_status.yml:797 and scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:21402
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The implementation compares the issue author against GH_PAT's login (`UNMERGED_CLOSE_LOGIN` / `UNBLOCK_TRUSTED_LOGIN`), but `scripts/check_failure_triage.sh` posts triage issues using `CHECK_TRIAGE_ISSUES_TOKEN` (.github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml:687), whose owner can differ. When the owners differ, `check_triage_target_branch` returns None, both paths reject the marker (`no_trusted_marker` / `non_target_base`), and the issue stays open. The agents.d/8955 fragment documents this as a known limitation, but no code path enforces or handles the mismatch.
- requirement: Add the helper and its unit tests in scripts/orchestrate_lib.py.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The test failure report confirms that tests/test_orchestrate_lib.py is failing. The task requires a verified implementation, not just the presence of failing test code.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
